title: Perineuronal Net Mapping and Quantification with Quint
author: Joseph Martin

1. Create a "Quint" folder on your C drive for all software installation 2. Download all software from the following links: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/powertoys/install (We used PowerToysUserSetup-0.85.1-x64) https://www.nitrc.org/projects/nutil/ (We used nutil_win_v.0.8.0) https://www.nitrc.org/projects/quicknii (See below) https://www.nitrc.org/projects/visualign (We used VisuAlign-v0_9) https://www.ilastik.org/documentation/basics/installation (We used version 1.2.0.post1-gpu) Make sure to install the appropriate QuickNII atlas version for your images Mice: We used ABAMouse-v3-2017 Rats: We used WHSRat-v4 3. Unzip all downloads within the "Quint" folder that you created 4. If desired, create desktop shortcuts for each software program or pin them to the task bar 5. Open all software programs to ensure that they are functional

steps.title: Initial Image Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the directory structure and organize raw image files for processing.

substeps.instruction: Download and duplicate the QUINT Template Folders. For sagittal sections, use both 'Left' and 'Right' folders as separate brains.
Obtain images (typically TIFFs) and place them in the 'A. Original TIFFs' folder (or 'AA. Original TIFFs, Images Excluded' if quality control was performed).
Ensure images are ordered and oriented: Coronal (rostral to caudal, dorsal top, left on left); Sagittal (lateral to medial, dorsal top, rostral left).
Copy images from folder A (or AA) into 'B. Renamed TIFFs'.

steps.title: Rename Images with PowerRename
steps.instruction: Standardize filenames to ensure compatibility with Quint software.

substeps.instruction: Use PowerRename to replace all periods, hyphens, and hashtags in filenames with underscores (set 'apply to' to 'Filename only').
Add a serialized number '_sXXX' (e.g., _s001) to the end of each filename by setting 'apply to' to 'Filename + extension', replacing '.tif' with '_s${padding=3,start=1}.tif'.

steps.title: Resize Images and Generate XML
steps.instruction: Downsize images using Nutil and verify compatibility with FileBuilder.

substeps.instruction: In Nutil, create a new 'Resize' project. Set Input Folder to 'B. Renamed TIFFs' and Output Folder to 'C. PNGs (with section numbers)'.
Set Resize Type to 'Percent' and Resize Factor to 85 for coronal or 60 for sagittal.
Save the resize file to 'C. PNGs (with section numbers)' and click 'Start'.
Open FileBuilder, navigate to 'C. PNGs (with section numbers)', select all images, and click 'Open'.
Verify that all remarks in the rightmost column are green or orange. If red, repeat the resize process, decreasing the Resize Factor by 10 (75 coronal / 50 sagittal) until all are green or orange.
Select 'Save XML', name the file by cohort/condition, and save it to 'D. QuickNII'.
Copy and paste all PNGs from 'C.' to 'D.'.

steps.title: Configure QuickNII
steps.instruction: Set up the QuickNII environment for atlas mapping.

substeps.instruction: Open the species-appropriate version of QuickNII.
Go to 'Manage Data' and load the XML file from the 'D.' folder.
Double-click an image filename in the data management window to load it into the mapping window.
Open 'Values and Control' in the bottom left of the mapping window.
For sagittal sections: change 'Coronal' to 'Sagittal'.
Adjust 'Image Darkness' slider if images are too dark.
For mice: select 'Outline' and set atlas type to 'Rainbow 2017' or 'Original 2017'.

For sagittal sections: use the bottom-right window to ensure left hemisphere tissues are on the left and right on the right; set angles in red, green, and blue boxes to 0 or 180 for correct orientation (dorsal top, rostral left).

steps.title: Map Images in QuickNII
steps.instruction: Align images to the atlas using a strategic sampling approach.

substeps.instruction: Select ~3 images with clear landmarks distributed across the axis to map first.
Choose viewing mode: For mice, use STPt avg 2015 (initial) and Rainbow 2017 with Outline (refinement). For rats, use MRI (initial) and Segmentation with Outline (refinement).
Adjust atlas opacity using the slider; use 'H' for image only and 'V' for atlas only.
Perform alignment based on section type:

Coronal: Adjust rostrocaudal position (red dot in Horizontal View), mediolateral linear translation (drag atlas left/right), mediolateral scaling (spacebar for reference point, then double-headed left-right arrow), dorsoventral linear translation (drag atlas up/down), dorsoventral scaling (spacebar for reference point, then double-headed up-down arrow), rotation (curved arrows), rostrocaudal angle change (yellow line in Coronal View), and dorsoventral angle change (yellow line in Horizontal View).

Sagittal: Adjust mediolateral position (red dot in Horizontal View), rostrocaudal linear translation (drag atlas left/right), rostrocaudal scaling (spacebar for reference point, then double-headed left-right arrow), dorsoventral linear translation (drag atlas up/down), dorsoventral scaling (spacebar for reference point, then double-headed up-down arrow), rotation (curved arrows), mediolateral angle change (yellow line in Coronal View), and dorsoventral angle change (yellow line in Horizontal View).
Use landmarks: Coronal (Anterior Commissure, Lateral Ventricles, Hippocampus); Sagittal (Hippocampus, Piriform cortex).
Click 'Store' to save the mapped image and apply changes to remaining images. Repeat until all are mapped.

steps.title: Finalize QuickNII Mapping
steps.instruction: Verify mapping linearity and export data.

substeps.instruction: Check the graph in the data management window; it should be approximately linear and monotonic.
Click 'Save JSON', name the file, and save it to 'D. QuickNII'.
Exit QuickNII.

steps.title: Non-linear Transformation in VisuAlign
steps.instruction: Refine the atlas alignment using markers to correct local distortions.

substeps.instruction: Copy all PNGs from 'C. PNGs with Section Numbers' to 'E. VisuAlign'.
Open VisuAlign, open the QuickNII JSON file from 'D.', and set the opacity slider to the right to show the atlas as an outline.
For each image: add markers (spacebar) to areas that are already well-mapped to 'lock' them, then add markers to areas needing adjustment (starting with tissue outline, then moving inward).
Ensure key landmarks (hippocampus, ventricles, cortex/corpus callosum differentiation, cortical layers) are aligned. Limit to ~50 annotations per image.
Navigate images using single arrows (top right).
Save the final state as a JSON file in 'E. VisuAlign'.
Select 'File' -> 'Export' and save to 'E. VisuAlign'.
Copy all '.flat' files from 'E. VisuAlign' to the 'Atlas_Maps' folder within 'I. Nutil'.

steps.title: Pixel Classification in Ilastik
steps.instruction: Train a model to classify PNN intensity levels.

substeps.instruction: Copy PNGs from 'C. PNGs with Section Numbers' to 'G. Ilastik/A. Images'.
In Ilastik, create a 'Pixel Classification' project. Upload representative training images (at least 1 per brain/condition) and select 'Copy into project file'.
In 'Feature selection', select all white boxes (turn them green).

In 'Training', add labels and set colors: Label 1 (high-intensity PNNs): bright green; Label 2 (moderate-intensity PNNs): dark green; Label 3 (diffuse PNN signal): bright blue; Label 4 (background): dark blue.
Determine high-intensity PNNs by opening training images in ImageJ, setting contrast to maximum, and labeling only clearly-defined PNNs as Label 1.
Annotate training images by drawing on pixels for each label. Use 'Live Update' and 'Segmentation' views to refine. Focus on blue 'Uncertainty' areas.
Save the Ilastik project.
In 'Prediction Export', set source to 'Probabilities' and format to 'hdf5'.
In 'Batch Processing', select all images in 'G. Ilastik/A. Images', process them, and move resulting 'Probabilities.h5' files to 'B. Probabilities (Pixel Classification)'.

steps.title: Object Classification in Ilastik
steps.instruction: Identify individual PNN objects based on pixel predictions.

substeps.instruction: In Ilastik, create an 'Object Classification [Inputs: Raw Data, Pixel Prediction Map]' project.
Upload the same training images and their corresponding probability files from 'B. Probabilities (Pixel Classification)', selecting 'Copy into project file'.
In 'Threshold and Size Filter', set: Method 'Simple', Input '0', Smooth '0.6', Threshold '0.5', Size filter Min '0' and Max '400'. Click 'Apply'.
In 'Object Feature Selection', select 'Standard Object Features' but deselect 'Bounding Box Maximum', 'Bounding Box Minimum', and 'Center of the Object'.
In 'Object Information Export', set source to 'Object Identities' and format to 'tiff'.
In 'Batch Processing', select all raw images from 'A. Images' and their corresponding probability files from 'B. Probabilities (Pixel Classification)'.
Process all files and move 'Object Identities' files to 'G. Ilastik/C. Object Identities (Object Classification)'.

steps.title: Convert Object Identity Files
steps.instruction: Change the color of object identity files using an ImageJ macro for quantification.

substeps.instruction: Open ImageJ/Fiji. Set input folder to 'C. Object Identities (Object Classification)' and output folder to 'D. Object Identities Post-Color Change' with format 'PNG'.
Run the 'object color change macro' from 'G. Ilastik'. Update the macro file path to the 'ALL GREEN LUT.lut' file on your computer (use forward slashes).
Click 'Process' in the Batch Process window.
Copy all files from 'D. Object Identities Post-Color Change' to the 'Segmentation' folder within 'I. Nutil'.

steps.title: Quantification with Nutil
steps.instruction: Quantify PNNs by overlaying segmentations with atlas maps.

substeps.instruction: In Nutil, create a new 'Quantifier' project. Set Analysis type to 'Quint'.
Set the segmentation folder to 'I. Nutil/Segmentation' and the atlas maps folder to 'I. Nutil/Atlas_Maps'.
Set Reference Atlas to 'Allen Mouse Brain 2017' (mice) or 'WHS Atlas Rat v4' (rats).
Select the final VisuAlign JSON file from 'E. VisuAlign' and set the output folder to 'I. Nutil/Output'. Set Output Reports to 'All'.
Set the object color for Label 1: Open a segmentation image in Fiji, use 'Pick screen color' in Nutil to select the bright green color (HTML: #00ff00).
Set Object splitting to 'No', Minimum object size to '1', Pixel scale to '1', Pixel scale unit to 'pixels', and Custom masks to 'No'.
Set Output report type to 'HTML' and Customized reports to 'Custom', selecting the 'updated selected-brain-regions.txt' file.
Set Coordinate extraction to 'All', Point cloud density to '1', Display object IDs to 'No', Display region IDs to 'Yes', and Unique ID format to '_sXXX'.
Save the Nutil analysis file in 'I. Nutil' and click 'Start'. Repeat for each hemisphere/condition.

steps.title: 3D Visualization with MeshView
steps.instruction: Visualize the quantified PNN coordinates in a 3D brain model.

substeps.instruction: Open the species-appropriate MeshView link.
Upload the 'PROJECTNAME_3D_combined.json' file from 'I. Nutil/Output/Coordinates'.
Adjust atlas mesh opacity using the left panel (e.g., 'All' slider far left, 'Root' slider at 20% for translucency).
Toggle specific PNN brain regions using the right panel sliders.
